claims.finding: Broadcom is reported to be raising $70-80bn of debt (senior tranche ~$45bn, junior ~$35bn) through an SPV that buys the chips and leases them back to AI customers including Anthropic, scaling up a $35bn Anthropic compute commitment unveiled in June - and there is no 8-K, S-3 or 424B anywhere in the 400-day filing index to confirm it, the last 8-K of any kind being 2026-07-06.

claims.why_not_priced: The stock moved about 1% on the report and the coverage framed it purely as balance-sheet and credit risk (the article's own analyst quote is that the residual guarantee 'is where the risk sits'). Nobody has run it the other way: a lessor does not arrange $70-80bn of chip-lease paper for chips that have not been ordered, so the financing is a leading indicator of bookings. Meanwhile the pre-print preview coverage in this same corpus anchors readers on 'AI bookings and backlog exceeded $30 billion entering the quarter' and '$60 billion cumulative', and the print is the first forum where the company has to size either the backlog or the financing. If the market had already made this link the stock would not have kept sliding to -12.2% over 20 days while the AI demand datapoints in the corpus (OpenAI as fourth XPU customer at 10GW, Apple custom chip extended to 2031, supply locked through 2028, Tan's June math of ~$19bn H1 AI revenue doubling in H2) all pointed up. The band crosses zero because the same fact read as leverage plus a residual guarantee on an Anthropic-exposed SPV is a negative, and because Broadcom has never filed it.
claims.independence: Corroborated from a different source in the corpus: the Q2 FY26 call transcript has Hock Tan putting H1 AI revenue at 'something in the range of $19 billion' and telling analysts to 2x that for H2, https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/06/03/broadcom-avgo-q2-2026-earnings-transcript/ (docs/6970c7b2411041aebc1a1194edd46e45102511f7.txt), which is an implied ~$38bn H2 against a Q3 bar of 'AI revenue to exceed $16B' and therefore requires a very large Q4 AI number. A third, snippet-only pointer the same way: https://www.benzinga.com/markets/prediction-markets/26/08/61219624/broadcom-ai-financing-370-billion.
